Emerson Spice Hotel
Skip to content
Emerson Spice Hotel
The Heartbeat of Heritage
Welcome to our
magical spaces
Emerson Spice is a UNESCO World Heritage site and award winning boutique hotel located in the very heart of Stone Town, Zanzibar. Situated in a lovingly restored Swahili mansion, we host twelve uniquely decorated rooms, a renowned rooftop Tea House restaurant and our Secret Garden Restaurant.
DISCOVER STONE TOWN
Perfect Location
▪ In the historic centre of Stone Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
▪ Restored 19th‑century palace.
▪ 8 km (15–20 minutes) drive from Zanzibar International Airport.
▪ 8 minutes walk from the seafront.
▪ Surrounded by iconic landmarks, markets, museums, and winding alleys full of culture.
Food & Beverages
The hotel has two iconic restaurants, offering a refined and culinary experience for all tastes.
The Teahouse rooftop restaurant has stunning views of Stone Town.
The Secret Garden located in a tranquil inner courtyard is simply magical.
Timeless Culture
▪ Set within Stone Town’s living museum of Swahili, Arab, Persian, and Indian heritage
▪ Surrounded by centuries‑old architecture, carved doors, hidden courtyards, and historic alleyways
▪ Moments from traditional markets, artisan workshops, and the daily rhythm of Zanzibari life
Unique Rooms
Looking for a place to stay in Stone Town to experience the real Zanzibar?
All our twelve rooms are unique with their own opulent Swahili décor, colors and personality. Staying with us is to step into history where timeless elegance meets magical spaces.
ALL ROOMS
Our Partners
Our Restaurants
We host two renowned restaurants. Our Secret Garden offers lunch, dinner, live music and events. All amongst chandeliers and tropical foliage in the enchanted ruins of our ancient garden.
Our rooftop Tea House offers Swahili high tea, lunch and dinner with spectacular views and sunsets overlooking historical Stone Town. Always accompanied by the call to prayer from the mosques and temples below.

Stone Town cultural experiences
More than a change of scenery, a return to the heartbeat of Stone Town. Footsteps drift through winding alleys and the scent of Zanzibar spices fills the air. Dhow sails glow against the Indian Ocean at sunset, musicians play in hidden courtyards, and the city’s stories unfold with every turn. Each moment invites you to connect with Stone Town, its people, flavours and its timeless culture.

Where is Kappa Senses Zanzibar located?
Kappa Senses Zanzibar is located in Pwani Mchangani, North-East Zanzibar, directly on a pristine white-sand beach overlooking the Indian Ocean. The resort is approximately 45 minutes from Abeid Amani Karume International Airport (ZNZ) and offers easy access to Stone Town, Mnemba Atoll, and other key attractions.
What types of rooms are available at Kapa Senses Zanzibar?
Kappa Senses Zanzibar features contemporary and spacious room categories, including Prestige Garden Rooms and Sea View Rooms, designed with modern comfort and elegant coastal aesthetics. Select categories offer direct sea views, while others are surrounded by lush tropical gardens.
What facilities and experiences does Kappa Senses Zanzibar offer?
The resort offers a large swimming pool, direct beach access, multiple restaurants and bars including a rooftop lounge, wellness and spa facilities, water sports options, and curated island experiences. The setting is ideal for couples, families, and groups seeking a stylish beachfront escape.
When is the best time to visit Kappa Senses Zanzibar?
Zanzibar is a year-round destination. The best weather is typically from June to October and December to March, offering warm temperatures, low rainfall, and ideal beach conditions. The resort is perfectly positioned to enjoy Zanzibar’s tropical climate throughout the year.

Accommodation
The Heartbeat of Heritage
Every room is unique
Emerson Spice Hotel is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Our lovingly restored Swahili mansion was originally owned by the Mwinyi Mkuu, the last Swahili ruler of Zanzibar.
All our twelve rooms are unique with their own opulent Swahili décor, colors and personality. Staying with us is to step into history where timeless elegance meets magical spaces.
Check Availability and Book Direct
Aida
Description
Décor
Amenities
Description
Inspired by the grand opera Aida by Giuseppe Verdi, this grandiose room has monumental archways, massive walls, soaring ceilings, stained glass doors and windows.
Décor
A large queen size bed with carved lions’ feet dominates the main room. Another queen size bed is placed in the adjacent space with a spiral staircase up to a mezzanine loft that has two single beds. The hand painted murals depict scenes from the famed opera.
Three full length stained glass windows are opening to our inner courtyard and French balconies, letting in a soft colorful light.
Aida is a duplex suitable for couples, a group of friends or a family with children. Separate and enclosed bathroom with large veranda facing our garden is found on the first level.
Amenities
All our rooms are equipped with air conditioning.
Our bathrooms are supplied with handwoven cotton kikoi towels and handmade organic soaps.
We also offer ecofriendly shampoo, conditioner and shower gel from Inaya Zanzibar.
All rooms have a fridge, complimentary drinking water and a coffee station with selected teas and coffee.

Description
This top-floor west-facing room is named after the main character and heroine in William Shakespeare’s Othello. Our founder Emerson Dewey Skeens loved Guiseppe Verdis’ opera based on the play and dedicated this space to Desdemona; the beautiful, intelligent daughter of a Venetian senator who defies societal norms and elopes with Othello.
The room presides over Stone Town as from a castle’s tower with view of the cityscape. Desdemona’s piety and prayers inspired Emerson to collect some pieces from the Anglican cathedral when they were being discarded in renovations.
Décor
A prier bench sits between the two French balcony doors, and in the bathroom, a variation of Gothic stained glass windows afford privacy and light.

Discover Stone Town

Discover Stone Town
Cultural Zanzbari Heritage
Climate, History, Culture and Beauty of Zanzibar
Zanzibar is not just a tropical island destination — it’s an experience shaped by centuries of trade, culture, warm Indian Ocean waters, and some of the most striking beaches in East Africa. Whether you’re planning a romantic escape, a wellness retreat, or an all-inclusive beach holiday, here’s everything you need to know before visiting this Indian Ocean paradise.
Cultural Zanzbari Heritage
Where is Stone Town?
Stone Town is the historic old quarter of Zanzibar City, located on the western coast of Unguja Island, known for its winding alleys, carved doors, and centuries of Swahili, Arab, and Indian heritage.
UNESCO Heritage Site
UNESCO World Heritage Site for its cultural significance
Heart of Zanzibar’s history , trade, and architecture
Famous landmarks: House of Wonders, Old Fort, Forodhani Gardens
Built from coral stone , giving buildings their warm glow
Known for spices, markets, and traditional dhow culture
EMERSON SPICE HOTEL GUIDE
Travel Essentials in Stone Town
Visa: Most travellers can obtain a visa on arrival in Tanzania (check current regulations before travel). Currency: Tanzanian Shilling (USD widely accepted in resorts).
ATMs: Stone Town has several ATM s for withdrawing cash. Language: Swahili (English widely spoken in hotels and tourism). Flight time from Europe: Approx. 8–9 hours direct

Stone Town Seafront - dhows, sunsets & markets
Stone Town’s seafront is a breezy stretch of ocean views, dhows, sunsets, and lively waterfront atmosphere.
Why travellers love it:
Warm, golden sunsets over the Indian Ocean
Traditional dhows sailing past the promenade
Lively Forodhani night market with fresh seafood
Easy access to historic landmarks along the waterfront
Relaxed, breezy vibe perfect for strolling and people‑watching
EMERSON SPICE HOTEL GUIDE
Streets of Stone Town
Stone Town’s streets are a maze of narrow, twisting alleys filled with life, history, and atmosphere, a place where every turn feels like stepping deeper into Zanzibar’s story.
Coral‑stone buildings with carved wooden doors
Aromas of spices, coffee, and fresh bread
Local shops, markets, and hidden courtyards
Friendly street life with kids playing and vendors chatting
A blend of Swahili, Arab, and Indian architectural heritage
SWAHILI CULTURE
Experience & Celebrate Culture
Zanzibar’s culture is deeply influenced by Swahili traditions, blending African, Arab, and Indian heritage. Visitors will notice:
Warm hospitality
Modest dress customs in villages
Traditional dhow boats sailing at sunset
Fresh seafood and fragrant spice-infused cuisine
Respect for local customs enhances your experience and strengthens cultural connection.
ZANIBARI CULTURE CULTURE
Why Zanzibar Is More Than Just a Beach Destination
What makes Zanzibar special is its balance:
Natural beauty
Cultural depth
Sustainable tourism growth
Authentic coastal communities
Year-round warm climate
Whether exploring historic Stone Town, walking the sandy beaches, or relaxing under palm trees overlooking the Indian Ocean, Zanzibar offers both tranquillity and cultural richness.
It’s not simply somewhere you visit, it’s somewhere you feel.
Delicious Dining Choices
A celebration of Zanzibar’s flavours & soul
Set in the heart of Stone Town, Emerson Spice Hotel is a lovingly restored architectural gem where Zanzibar’s rich history, vibrant culture and artistic spirit come together. This boutique heritage hotel offers an immersive experience: atmospheric rooms filled with character, rooftop dining inspired by local flavours, and a setting that places you right amid the winding alleys, markets and stories of old Zanzibar. Created for travellers seeking authenticity and connection, Emerson Spice blends comfort, culture and creativity in a way that makes every stay feel meaningful.

What is Stone Town, really like?
It’s the part of Zanzibar where the island’s soul lives. When you walk these alleys, you’re walking through hundreds of years of trade, culture, and stories. We don’t see it as a “tourist site” - it’s our neighbourhood, our markets, our daily rhythm.
Stone Town is the old heart of Zanzibar City; a UNESCO World Heritage maze of coral‑stone houses, carved wooden doors, mosques, markets, and centuries of Swahili, Arab, Indian, and European history layered on top of each other.
Why is Stone Town famous?
Because it’s one of the best-preserved Swahili coastal cities in the world, with 500+ carved doors, Omani palaces, Indian merchant houses, and the site of the former slave market.
People come for the architecture, but they stay for the feeling. The call to prayer echoing through the alleys, kids playing football in tiny courtyards, the smell of cloves and grilled seafood - that mix is what makes Stone Town unforgettable.

Dining Experiences

Dining
STONE TOWN DINING EXPERIENCES
One hotel, two restaurants, countless experiences.
At Emerson Spice, dining is part of the experience.
Set in the heart of Stone Town, our two restaurants offer two very different ways to discover Zanzibar s flavours – from rooftop views and sunset cocktails to intimate meals in our own city oasis, surrounded by tropical greenery.
HIGHEST ROOFTOP TEA HOUSE
The Tea House
Lunch with a view. Swahili High Tea. Cocktails at sunset. Tasting menus after dark.
Perched on the rooftop of Emerson Spice, The Tea House Restaurant combines food, drinks and one of the best views over Stone Town.
Join us for a relaxed à la carte lunch , featuring fresh local ingredients and flavours inspired by the Swahili coast.
For a more leisurely afternoon, pre-order our Swahili High Tea , a selection of sweet and savoury bites inspired by the island's culinary traditions.
As the day turns to evening, the rooftop transforms into a magical setting for dinner under the stars. Discover our signature eight-course seafood tasting menu , with the option to add our carefully selected wine pairings.
Dinner is served promptly at 7:00pm , but we highly recommend arriving early to enjoy one of our signature cocktails and watch the sunset over the rooftops of Stone Town.
Whether you come for lunch, tea, a cocktail or dinner, The Tea House is all about taking your time, enjoying the view and experiencing Stone Town from above.

MAGICAL SPACE
The Secret Garden
A hidden garden in the heart of Stone Town.
Behind the old walls of Emerson Spice lies the Secret Garden – a lush, atmospheric restaurant tucked away from the bustle of the city.
Surrounded by tropical foliage, historic stone walls and a warm glow, the garden offers a relaxed setting for food, drinks and evenings under the stars.
Come during the day for a leisurely lunch, or return back in the evening for the Seafood BBQ. On Wednesdays and Fridays, the garden comes alive with live music from local Zanzibari artists.
The Secret Garden is also a place for the unexpected.
Throughout the year we host special dinners, cultural events, celebrations and other gatherings , bringing together food, music, art and the people who make Zanzibar a rich vibrant place.
For private occasions, the entire Secret Garden can be reserved for book launches, intimate dinners, weddings and celebrations. A separate private dining room and lounge can accommodate up to 14 guests seated, offering a more intimate setting for special gatherings.

Yes.
What types of rooms are available at Emerson Spice Hotel?
Emerson Spice Hotel offers a selection of individually designed boutique rooms and suites, each with its own character and story.
Guests can choose from beautifully restored heritage rooms, spacious luxury suites, and romantic rooftop rooms that capture the charm of Stone Town’s historic architecture. Every room is unique, featuring traditional Zanzibari décor, antique furnishings, and views over the old city or the hotel’s inner courtyard.
This variety gives travellers the freedom to pick a room that matches the experience they want, whether that is a grand Sultan‑style suite, an intimate historic chamber, or a room with a private veranda overlooking Stone Town.
What facilities and experiences does Emerson Spice Hotel offer?
Emerson Spice Hotel offers a blend of cultural, culinary and architectural experiences that reflect the spirit of Stone Town. Guests can enjoy beautifully restored heritage interiors, a peaceful inner courtyard, and individually designed rooms filled with antiques and Zanzibari craftsmanship. The hotel is also known for its exceptional dining. Its rooftop restaurant serves a daily tasting menu inspired by local spices and fresh island produce, along with sweeping views over Stone Town and the Indian Ocean.
